resultJson.description: Make IssueHandle.parse accept full GitHub issue/PR URLs in addition to the owner/repo#N short form, and update the user-facing docs in the flows that take an issue reference.

tasks.title: Extend IssueHandle.parse to accept GitHub URLs
tasks.description: In tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitHubTool.scala, extend IssueHandle.parse (and thereby parseOrThrow) to accept, besides the existing '<owner>/<repo>#<number>' short form, full GitHub URLs of the forms 'https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>' and 'https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/pull/<number>' (the pull form matters because flows/review.sc parses PR refs through IssueHandle). Tolerate: http or https scheme, an optional 'www.' prefix, an optional trailing slash, and surrounding whitespace — same leniency the current ShortRefPattern gives the short form. Do not attempt query strings or fragments. Update the Left error message so it names both accepted forms, and update the parse/parseOrThrow doc comments accordingly (usage-focused, concise, per repo comment conventions). Keep the method signatures unchanged — FlowCompilesTest.scala (runner/src/test/scala/flowtests/FlowCompilesTest.scala:248-249) compiles against them. Add a dedicated unit test file tools/src/test/scala/orca/tools/IssueHandleTest.scala (munit FunSuite, same style as OsGitHubToolTest.scala) covering: short form, short form with whitespace, https issues URL, https pull URL, http scheme, www prefix, trailing slash, and rejection cases (garbage, missing number, bare 'owner/repo'). Run the tools module tests to verify.

tasks.title: Update flow user docs to mention URL form
tasks.description: Update the user-facing documentation in the flows that accept an issue reference so they state both accepted input forms ('<owner>/<repo>#<number>' or a full GitHub issue URL like 'https://github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<number>'). Files and spots: flows/issue-pr.sc — line 1 header comment, the doc-comment intro (line 16), and the Usage section (lines 29-33, including the scala-cli example); flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc — line 1 header comment, doc-comment intro (line 18), and the Usage section (~line 46). flows/review.sc needs no change: its resolver agent already accepts URLs and normalizes to the short-ref before parsing. Keep the wording concise per repo doc conventions — one mention per spot, no repeated explanation. Also update the mirrored flow copy in docs only if compilation requires it; the FlowCompilesTest copies embed code, not doc comments, so they should not need changes. Verify by running the runner module's FlowCompilesTest (flows must still compile).

resultJson.brief:
Repo: Orca (direct-style Scala 3, sbt multi-module). MANDATORY: load the direct-style-scala skill via the Skill tool before writing or reviewing any Scala code (CLAUDE.md requirement — applies to you as a subagent).

Core change site: tools/src/main/scala/orca/tools/GitHubTool.scala. `case class IssueHandle(owner: String, repo: String, number: Int)` with companion `IssueHandle.parse(s: String): Either[String, IssueHandle]` and `parseOrThrow(s: String): IssueHandle` (throws OrcaFlowException, imported from the orca package). Current implementation is a single regex `ShortRefPattern = """\s*([^/\s]+)/([^#\s]+)#(\d+)\s*""".r` matched in `parse`. The change adds URL forms (github.com/<owner>/<repo>/issues/<n> and /pull/<n>) — a second regex alternative is the natural shape.

Consumers of parse (signatures must not change):
- flows/issue-pr.sc:44 and flows/issue-pr-bugfix.sc:60 — `IssueHandle.parseOrThrow(orcaArgs.userPrompt)` on the raw CLI arg; this is where users paste URLs today and get the parse error.
- flows/review.sc:108 — parses an agent-produced ref documented as short-form, then converts to PrHandle; PR URLs should therefore also parse (the /pull/ form).
- runner/src/test/scala/flowtests/FlowCompilesTest.scala:248-249, 488, 531 — compile-checks the API (`parseOrThrow("acme/widgets#7")` and `parse` returning Either[String, IssueHandle]).

Tests: munit FunSuite style; see tools/src/test/scala/orca/tools/OsGitHubToolTest.scala for conventions (plain `test("...")` + `assertEquals`). There is currently NO dedicated test for IssueHandle.parse — create tools/src/test/scala/orca/tools/IssueHandleTest.scala. Build/test commands are in CONTRIBUTING.md; sbt runs are slow (8–15 min), so scope test runs to the affected module (e.g. `sbt tools/test`, `sbt runner/test`).

Doc conventions (strict in this repo): comments are usage-focused, concise, no implementation history, no generic Scala/GitHub exposition; the locality test — only file-specific facts. The flows' doc comments are the primary 'user info': issue-pr.sc lines 1/16/29-33 and issue-pr-bugfix.sc lines 1/18/~46 currently say only `<owner>/<repo>#<number>`. Flows are scala-cli scripts pinned to the published `org.virtuslab::orca:0.1.2` dep — ignore version-compat concerns (project convention: consumers are version-pinned scripts).

Non-obvious: PrHandle (same file) has a `url` method producing `https://github.com/<o>/<r>/pull/<n>` — keep the accepted URL shapes consistent with it. The parse error message string ('expected ...') surfaces directly to flow users via OrcaFlowException, so it must name both accepted forms after the change.
